title: Reliability Scouts 90-day field sprint and activation notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic, lightweight 90-day field sprint for the "Reliability Scouts" cross-functional pilot. The goal is to validate an operational pattern for SLO adoption (small, fast, measurable) that can scale across product teams. This is intentionally low-friction: short experiments, concrete acceptance criteria, and clear escalation paths.

Principles:
- Start small: pick 2–3 candidate services with bounded blast radius.
- Measure what matters: pick 2 signals per service (user-facing latency and error rate).
- Short feedback loops: weekly metrics review + tactical fixes, biweekly rollout decisions.
- Automate where obvious: alerts -> runbook -> remediation script.
- Learn and iterate: capture what breaks, why, and how to prevent it.

High-level objectives (90 days):
1) Establish per-service SLOs and observable signal catalogs for 3 pilot services.
2) Deliver minimal dashboards and one automated alert per signal tied to a runbook.
3) Prove rollback and fallback behavior for degraded model-serving paths.
4) Produce a lightweight ops-contract template (service -> platform) with SLIs, ownership, and escalation.
5) Document lessons and a repeatable onboarding checklist for second cohort.

Candidate service selection criteria:
- <100 requests/sec typical, clear consumer impact, healthy commit cadence, product partner willing to participate.
- Proposed picks this sprint: ranking-service-v2, chat-router, embeddings-proxy (final selection in kickoff).

SLO / SLI definitions (examples):
- ranking-service-v2: Availability SLO = 99.95% successful responses (200/2xx) measured over 7d; Latency SLI = p95 < 120ms for inference-only requests over 7d window.
- chat-router: Availability SLO = 99.9% (7d); End-to-end latency SLI = p90 < 350ms (includes routing, not model).
- embeddings-proxy: Availability SLO = 99.8%; Token-usage anomaly SLI = baseline token/sec +- 3 sigma alert.

Success criteria (how we know the sprint worked):
- Each pilot service has an SLO, SLI, dashboard, and at least one automated alert wired to a runbook.
- At least one documented mitigation improved SLI by >15% (e.g., caching hit rate, batching policy).
- Ops contract template accepted by platform and 1 product area.
- Short "after-action" doc with actionable checklist created for next cohort.

Sprint timeline (weeks):
- Week 0 (Prep, 1 week): finalize service picks, stakeholder roster, and minimal metric definitions. Kickoff workshop.
- Week 1–2 (Instrumentation): ensure traces/metrics/logs are present, add SLI exporters if missing, derive baselines.
- Week 3 (Dashboard + Alerts): create dashboards, define alerts, attach preliminary runbooks.
- Week 4–6 (Mitigation experiments): implement 2 tactical mitigations per service (e.g., prefix cache, reduced batch-size for tail-latency), measure impact.
- Week 7–8 (Policy & Contract): draft ops contract, agree on ownership, define canary/fallback policy for rollouts.
- Week 9–12 (Hardening & Handoff): finalize automation, document playbooks, deliver handoff and retrospective.

Weekly cadence and checkpoints:
- Weekly 60-min "Scout Standup" (Mon): quick signal review, blockers, experiment status. Attendees: service owners, SRE lead, platform eng rep, observability engineer.
- Biweekly 90-min "Sprint Review" (every other Fri): demo mitigations, compare baseline vs current, adjust next actions.
- Ad-hoc incident sync if an alert crosses a predefined threshold (error budget burn >50% in 24h).

Roles & responsibilities:
- Reliability Scout (SRE lead - Aisha): program coordinator, runbook coach, assists instrumentation.
- Service Owner (product/eng): actionable owner for SLO decision, enacts mitigations, approves ops contract.
- Observability Engineer: dashboards, alerting rules, SLIs.
- Platform Engineer: provides primitives (caching, batching toggles, autoscale knobs).
- Solutions Eng / Support rep: validates customer-impact assumptions, helps craft communication.

Ops contract (minimum fields):
- Service name, team owner, SLO targets, SLIs and signal sources, oncall rotation, escalation path (pager -> slack -> SRE), expected remediation timeline, accepted mitigations and fallback. Template will be stored: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Ops+Contracts

Runbook template (to attach to each alert):
- Symptom and impact description
- First checks (logs/metrics/traces)
- Quick mitigation steps (toggle cache, roll to previous model variant, scale-up command)
- How to escalate (who to notify, criteria)
- Post-incident notes and retrospective link

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- Risk: Alert fatigue from noisy SLI definitions -> Mitigation: require 15–30m smoothing window + confidence suppression for transient spikes.
- Risk: Platform changes required are blocked on infra -> Mitigation: pick at least one mitigation that is config-only (feature flag).
- Risk: Product team cadence mismatch -> Mitigation: align on a single decision owner and weekly finance-booked meeting.

Instrumentation & dashboard checklist:
- Exporters in place for latency, error counts, and request volume.
- Traces include model inference span, routing span, and cache span.
- Dashboard panels: SLI trend (7d), error budget burn rate, top 5 failure types, p50/p95/p99 latency.
- Alert rule examples: p95 latency > SLI threshold for 10m, error rate > threshold for 5m with >100 requests.

Automation candidates (quick wins):
- Prefix cache for ranking-service-v2 (cache hit metric + TTL tuning).
- Adaptive batching policy toggle for embeddings-proxy (decrease batch size if p99 tail spikes).
- Lightweight request-level sampling to attach traces to spikes automatically.

Communication plan (internal + customer-facing):
- Internal: Scout Standup notes posted in #reliability-scouts and weekly summary to SRE-all@redwood.ai.
- Customer: For any user-visible regressions during pilot we draft a short status note template and have product comms review.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Which teams own SLA vs SLO language for these services? Need legal review if we expose any SLA-like commitments.
- Can platform provide a safe feature-flag service for immediate toggles? If not, need manual playbooks.
- Should we include cost-of-mitigation as a required field in the ops contract? (pro: transparency; con: slows sign-off)

Artifacts to produce by sprint end:
- SLO/SLI definitions doc per service (short, 1-pager).
- Dashboards and alert rules in the observability repo (PRs merged).
- Ops contract template signed by platform and one product team.
- Playbook + 1 mitigation script per service checked into runbook repo.
- Retrospective doc capturing metrics, what worked, and recommended changes.

Minimal onboarding checklist for next cohort (to include in alpha handbook):
- Confirm service pick and owner.
- Baseline SLIs collected for 7 days.
- Dashboard and 1 alert created.
- Runbook attached and verified by oncall.
- Two mitigation candidates scoped and prioritized.

Quick references and links:
- Reliability Scouts program page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Reliability+Scouts+Program
- Observability repo (dashboards): github.com/redwood-inference/observability/dashboards
- SRE runbooks folder: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbooks

Next steps (by Monday):
- Finalize service picks (Aisha + Jonah)
- Schedule kickoff workshop with product owners and platform (Priya)
- Create initial dashboard skeletons for ranking-service-v2 and chat-router (Sophie)
